name: Overhead Band Pull-Apart
description: The overhead band pull-apart starts with arms raised overhead holding a resistance band and pulls the band apart behind the head, training the rear deltoids and middle trapezius through an overhead pulling arc. This positioning creates different stress on the shoulder rotators compared to the standard chest-height pull-apart, challenging the external rotators in a more vulnerable and often undertrained overhead position.

execution.starting_position: Hold a resistance band with both hands wider than shoulder width. Raise arms overhead — band taut across the front overhead.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a very light band — the overhead position greatly increases mechanical disadvantage.
steps: Step 1: Begin with arms overhead, band taut.
Step 2: Pull the band apart by moving the hands outward and downward in an arc.
Step 3: Continue until the band reaches behind the head or at least behind the ears.
Step 4: Return to the overhead position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the pull-apart. Inhale returning.
common_mistakes: Using too strong a band — the overhead position significantly reduces load capacity
Bending the elbows — arms stay straight throughout
safety_considerations: Very light band tension — this is a mobility and shoulder health exercise
Stop if shoulder pain occurs at any point in the arc
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Band from overhead front to behind the head.
coaching_cues: Lead with the pinkies as you pull apart
Full arc — behind the head, not just beside
